hints: The shoelace formula gives twice the polygon area.
An edge with coordinate differences dx,dy contributes gcd(|dx|,|dy|) boundary points when endpoints are counted consistently.
Use Pick's theorem: area = interior + boundary/2 - 1.
analogy: The greatest common divisor counts equal lattice steps along an edge.
example: A 2 by 2 square has boundary 8 and interior 1, matching area 1+8/2-1=4.
algorithm: Sum cross products around the polygon and take absolute value A2. Sum gcd(abs(dx),abs(dy)) over edges to obtain boundary count B. Print (A2-B+2)/2 and B. Use a wide integer for the shoelace sum.
correctness: Each edge contains gcd(|dx|,|dy|) lattice steps; summing them counts each boundary vertex once. Pick's theorem then uniquely determines the interior count from area and boundary.
complexity: For n vertices and maximum coordinate difference C, O(n log C) time and O(n) space.
